name: Street-Custom Rebar Shiv 'Tetanus Kiss'
description:
A crude but effective stabbing weapon made from construction rebar ground to a point and wrapped in salvaged grip tape. The Tetanus Kiss is not a designed weapon — it is what happens when someone who cannot afford a Φ50 knife takes a piece of structural steel and makes it dangerous. The rebar's corrugated surface tears rather than cuts, creating ragged wounds that are extremely difficult to close and prone to infection.

The weapon's street name reflects its most feared characteristic: lower-tier medical facilities treat rebar puncture wounds with a specific dread, because the corrugated steel surface drags environmental contaminants — rust, concrete dust, biological matter — deep into the wound channel. Without immediate antimicrobial treatment, infection rates approach 80%. In GLMZ's lower tiers, where medical access is intermittent and expensive, a rebar puncture can kill through sepsis days after the initial injury.

The Tetanus Kiss exists because poverty is a weapon that creates weapons. Every piece of rebar in GLMZ's lower tiers is a potential armament, requiring only motivation and a grinding wheel to transform. Security forces who patrol lower-tier corridors have learned that confiscating improvised weapons is futile — the raw materials are literally the walls and floors.
legality: Illegal — improvised weapon, no registration possible
specifications:
blade_length: 15-30 cm (varies)
weight: 200-600 g (varies)
material: Construction rebar, various grades
edge_type: Ground point, corrugated shaft
infection_risk: Extremely high without immediate treatment
cost: Effectively free — salvaged materials
tactical_use: The Tetanus Kiss is a desperation weapon used by individuals who have no other options. Its corrugated surface and infection potential make it more dangerous than its crude appearance suggests — even a non-fatal puncture can become lethal without treatment that the attacker knows the victim likely cannot afford. Some lower-tier fighters deliberately do not clean their rebar weapons, relying on the infection threat as a force multiplier. The weapon has no defensive utility and minimal reach, making it useful only in ambush, surprise, or extreme close quarters.
cultural_context: The rebar shiv is GLMZ's most honest weapon — it is poverty made sharp. Its existence in every lower-tier district is a constant reminder that the city's economic stratification creates violence at the foundation. Social workers, medical professionals, and the rare corporate executive who visits the lower tiers all recognize the Tetanus Kiss as a symptom rather than a problem. Proposals to restrict access to construction materials have been dismissed as absurd, though they resurface periodically in tone-deaf policy discussions.
story_hooks: A rebar shiv has been recovered that was deliberately contaminated with a weaponized bacterial agent — someone is using the Tetanus Kiss tradition as a delivery mechanism for biological weapons.

A lower-tier community has organized a program to exchange rebar weapons for carbon-lattice knives — trading up from desperate to functional. The program is working, which has attracted attention from both supporters and people who do not want the lower tiers armed with anything effective.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutally utilitarian stabbing weapon—roughly tapered steel rod culminating in a ground point. The shaft retains visible corrugation from its original construction material, creating a deliberate texture that defines its lethality. Wrapped grip section shows irregular layering of salvaged grip tape in mismatched colors. Appears hastily finished but deliberately sharpened.
physical_description.dimensions: 15-30 cm total length (blade 10-20 cm, grip 5-10 cm); roughly 8-12 mm diameter at shaft, tapering to 2-3 mm point
physical_description.weight_description: Compact and balanced despite crude construction; feels weighty for its size due to steel density. Hefty enough to generate force in close quarters, light enough for extended concealment.
physical_description.primary_material: Construction-grade rebar steel (likely recycled/salvaged from GLMZ infrastructure)
physical_description.finish: Heavily oxidized and pitted; surface shows rust bloom in irregular patches. Ground point area has worn, exposed metal with dull sheen. Corrugations create shadow patterns along the shaft.
physical_description.color_scheme: Predominant oxidized rust-brown with patches of darker gunmetal gray. Grip tape in contrasting salvaged colors—typically faded neon, industrial yellow-green, or worn black electrical tape layered unevenly
physical_description.grip_texture: Multiple overlapping strips of salvaged grip tape (skateboard, tool handles, worn clothing tape)—textured and slightly tacky, designed for desperate retention rather than comfort. Tape edges may be frayed or peeling.
distinctive_features: Visible corrugations along full shaft length—intentionally preserved for wound trauma
Irregular grinding marks visible near point where stone/wheel contacted steel unevenly
Dark oxidation stains and rust bloom—some areas deliberately unwashed to propagate infection risk
Crude point—not symmetrical; angled from off-center grinding
Grip tape seams and overlaps visible; multiple color layers showing material scarcity
Possible small notches or scoring in shaft from being honed on concrete or stone
No markings, serial numbers, or manufacturer identification
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: None. Occasionally faint stamped numbers or construction codes from original rebar may be partially visible under rust, but deliberately worn or ground away by maker.
physical_description.condition_typical: Weathered and deliberately neglected. Rust and oxidation are features, not flaws. Grip tape shows signs of repeated handling and sweat damage. Sharp point maintained through occasional honing on concrete. Overall appearance suggests it has drawn blood.
